monthly_review.summary: Pace slowed and physiological efficiency declined sharply this month despite higher average heart rate, signaling fatigue rather than fitness gain.
monthly_review.highlight: The 20-bpm cadence drop (149 → 129 spm) and simultaneous 14-bpm HR rise strongly indicate neuromuscular fatigue overriding any small efficiency gain — this is not sustainable progress.

goal_tracker.message: Chasing last month’s volume (34.6 km across 7 sessions) is medically inadvisable given compromised readiness: the 5.0% aerobic decoupling and HR/cadence dysregulation on 2026-09-06 confirm systemic fatigue — prioritizing recovery now prevents injury and preserves long-term adaptation.

insights.title: Cadence collapse correlates with HR elevation and decoupling
insights.body: On 2026-09-06, cadence fell to 90 spm (lowest in dataset) while avg HR rose to 158 bpm and aerobic TE hit 5.0% — classic signs of central fatigue impairing motor unit recruitment and metabolic regulation.

insights.title: Efficiency improved slightly but at high physiological cost
insights.body: Running economy improved from 14.12 to 13.12 ml/kg/km (−1.00), yet occurred alongside +14 bpm HR and +0.6% aerobic TE — suggesting compensation via inefficient pacing or gait disruption rather than true aerobic adaptation.

insights.title: Training shifted dramatically into Zone 4 (46% this month vs 8% last month)
insights.body: Zone 4 volume surged from 8% to 46% of total time-in-zone while Z1 collapsed from 43% to 1%, eliminating foundational aerobic stimulus — this explains rising HR, falling cadence, and decoupling without VO2max improvement (VO2max remains stable at 39–40).

insights.title: Longest run increased while recovery metrics deteriorated
insights.body: Longest run grew from 12.0 km (Aug) to 10.7 km (Sep), yet aerobic TE jumped from 3.5% (2026-08-09) to 5.0% (2026-09-06) — indicating diminished fatigue resistance despite similar distance, likely due to inadequate low-intensity recovery between hard efforts.

recommendations.action: Zone 1 walk-run: 30 min total, HR ≤ 120 bpm, 2 min walk / 1 min jog x 10 cycles, Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Restores parasympathetic tone without cardiovascular or neuromuscular stress; cadence and HR data show current tolerance for sustained effort is severely reduced.

recommendations.action: Complete rest with guided breathing: 10 min box breathing (4-4-4-4) upon waking and before bed, Thursday
recommendations.reason: HRV and recovery balance are unmeasured but implied compromised by elevated resting HR trends and decoupling — autonomic retraining is the highest-leverage intervention available.

recommendations.action: Mobility & gait reset: 15 min barefoot drills (ankle circles, single-leg balance, glute bridges) + 5 min cadence-focused striders at 160 spm, Saturday
recommendations.reason: Cadence dropped 20 spm month-over-month; neuromuscular re-education at low load rebuilds stride integrity without triggering decoupling.

risk_flags.evidence: 46% Zone 4 time-in-zone (vs 8% last month), +14 bpm avg HR, 5.0% aerobic TE on longest run, cadence collapse to 90 spm
risk_flags.action: Remove all Zone 3+ efforts for 7 days; reintroduce only after cadence stabilizes ≥140 spm and aerobic TE ≤3.0% on 8+ km run.

risk_flags.evidence: Stride length remained stable (77.22 cm on 2026-09-06) despite cadence dropping to 90 spm — implying overstriding and increased ground contact time (327 ms, up from 282–307 ms in prior runs)
risk_flags.action: Pause all speedwork and hill running until cadence recovers to ≥140 spm and vertical oscillillation stabilizes ≤8.0 cm.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize vagal tone restoration and movement quality over volume or pace — the data shows fatigue has disrupted both cardiac regulation and motor control.
